problemStatement: A person who is not technical has no safe way to run a capable AI personal assistant on their own Mac: today it takes someone technical to install it, keep it running and keep it safe. Squire packages the source assistant, improved and made generic, as a Mac install that such a person sets up alone, on their own Claude plan, with safety on from the start.
objectives: A Squire owner who is not technical sets Squire up on a fresh Mac and gets a first reply, without Terminal.
Nothing is sent, published, deleted, overwritten, installed or spent without the Squire owner's yes for that one thing.
The Squire owner's secrets stay in the Mac's Keychain, and their personal details never reach a website or a support ticket.
One Squire session is always running, reachable from the Claude app on the Mac and on the phone.
Squire looks after itself: signed updates with rollback, a nightly backup, and fixing itself before offering a ticket.
Squire knows the Squire owner's Claude plan, paces itself and warns before big jobs.
executiveSummary: Squire packages the improved, generic reference assistant for Mac. It is for an owner who is not technical, on macOS 13 or later with 4 GB of memory and a Claude Pro plan or above. The core is free for ever; no paid feature is built in v0.1. Squire is free and source-available under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, and the Squire owner pays Claude directly. Business tools, paid features and other systems are out, and the maintainer's own platform code never ships.
targetUsers: A Squire owner: a person who is not technical, on a Mac with macOS 13 or later and 4 GB of memory or more, with a Claude Pro plan or above.
outOfScope: Business tools: invoices, payments, client sign-off, a business hub and client folders.
Paid add-on packs, a set-it-up-for-me service and any other paid feature.
Merging an owner's overlay with a changed core file (v0.1 offers keep yours or take the new one).
Admin tools and an admin session.
A GitHub account, deploy key or git sync on the Squire owner's Mac.
An encrypted secrets vault file or a .env file (secrets live in the Mac's Keychain).
Promises about connected services (mail, calendar, documents, design and social tools).
Ads, selling data and any mark-up on Claude usage.
Apple notarisation of the installer (parked); releases are signed by Stravica.
Plain words, short answers and a teach-me mode as criteria: they are reviewed behaviour, not tested.
constraints: Mac only: macOS 13 or later and 4 GB of memory or more.
A Squire owner needs a Claude Pro plan or above; the free Claude plan does not include Claude Code.
Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Squire is free and source-available, never described as open source.
The core is free for ever. No ads, no data sold, no mark-up on Claude usage.
Squire's code is Python and Swift, run by launchd agents. Node is used only for the development tool and never ships.
No code from the maintainer's own platform enters this repository.
inScope: A1. Core and the Squire owner's folder kept apart

A7. Wake-ups that find their own session
A8. Voice notes, transcribed on the Mac
A9. Pages on the Mac only, with the comment panel
A10. The home dashboard
A11. Looks after itself: health check, one-click restart, nightly iCloud backup, guided fixes
A12. Websites: the one-off safe Cloudflare set-up, a deploy-only token, preview first, live on yes
A13. Knows its Claude plan and paces itself
A14. Signed updates: plain-words changelog, yes first, health check, rollback
A15. Deep research, always warned first
A16. Build me an app: a one-page brief, coding standards, plan, build, test, preview, ship
A17. Video and audio: YouTube captions and the Squire owner's own files
A18. A browser it can drive: its own window, never signs in without a yes
A19. Safety, always on
A20. Support: self-fix first, ticket preview, the intake and the private tracker
A21. The public repository: fresh, with a pre-push privacy scan and a resale-stopping licence
